correctness.rationale: Independently derived the criterion in RESULT.md (1): the left and right derivatives of the convex function ||u+tv||_1 at zero are A−B and A+B, with A the signed sum on supp(u) and B the sum of absolute values off it, so zero is a minimizer exactly when |A|≤B. An axis forces every neighbor to lie in the complementary two-plane (apply the criterion in the reverse direction); at most two mutual lines fit in that plane because a full-support line there has just one possible outgoing orthogonal line, and there are just two axes otherwise. With a full-support line normalized to (a,b,c)>0, every two-support neighbor is the balanced difference on its support; any full-support neighbor has a sign type corresponding to a=b+c, b=a+c, or c=a+b. At most one such equality holds, and lines of the same sign type are not adjacent. This bounds that case by five. Among only two-supported lines each support has at most one per sign type, and a mutual pair on one support forces both lines to be balanced by the two directional equations. All six prescribed lines are adjacent in pairs: same-support sums cancel, and different supports give equality of shared and off-support magnitudes. Thus the proof covers all real projective lines and yields literal uniqueness. CHECK.py was inspected, not executed; its finite clique check is corroborative, and its derivative test compares equivalent signed-support expressions, not an independent continuous computation.
